\n- **Formato:** JPG, JPEG ou PNG, até 3:
- **Format:** JPG, JPEG, or PNG, up to 30 MB and 24 megapixels. Prefer the original file without excessive compression.
- **Whole, sharp object:** leave a margin around the part and avoid cropping its base or top. Aim for at least 500 pixels along its longest dimension; this is guidance, not an accuracy guarantee.
- **Simple, contrasting background:** a dark part on a light background, or a light part on a dark background. Avoid strong shadows, reflections, transparency, and objects touching its silhouette.
- **Aligned camera:** face the intended profile with the camera centered on the part, without tilting. Move farther away and use optical zoom when available to reduce perspective.
- **Known measurement:** use a measured part dimension or a ruler in the same plane. Mark two points and enter their actual distance in millimeters; pixels alone do not provide physical measurements.
- **Revolution / end cap:** use the side view of a part with axial symmetry. Draw or select only one side between the axis and the outer edge. The internal socket requires its own measurements.
- **Extrusion:** photograph a flat face perpendicularly, with a profile that stays constant along the depth. Enter the depth separately.
- **Complex shapes:** oblique views, organic parts, and hidden surfaces need additional views, measurements, and assisted reconstruction. A single photo cannot automatically recover the entire part.

If detection fails, adjust the crop, contrast, and thresholds, or draw and edit the points manually. Colored annotations are drawing references, not measurements. Always check the profile and dimensions before generating the solid.
